title: AI call screeners hide paying consumers. proAgent gets through. -
summary: On a subprime auto lender’s program, calls an AI call screener answered first added 25.8% to payments set up. Most dialers hang up on those calls. What that costs, and how proAgent waits for the customer instead.
body_markdown:
On a subprime auto lender’s outbound program, calls that an AI call screener answered first produced $17,755 in payments set up over three weeks. Calls where a person picked up directly set up $68,822, so screened calls added another 25.8%1. A dialer’s answering machine detection (AMD) would have hung up on every one of those screened calls.


Most dialers read a screener as an answering machine and disconnect, so the customer behind it never hears from the lender.


## Three weeks of screened calls


The lender switched on screener handling on October 12. By November 2, 2,081 of 25,780 outbound calls (8.1%) had reached a call screener. proAgent got past the screener to the customer on 170 of those calls (8.2%), and 27 of the 170 customers (16%) set up a payment1.

## Why AMD hangs up on screeners


Dialers were built to protect agent time. Predictive dialing passes through only the calls a person answers, and AMD drops anything that sounds like a machine before a human agent hears it. That made sense when fewer than 5% of answered calls had a real person on the line3.


One large collections agency even staffed a team in South Africa to call through voicemails and screeners and transfer live consumers to collectors onshore.


Some vendors now sell “smart” AMD that can tell a screener from a voicemail. Knowing it’s a screener doesn’t help much when the next move is still to hang up, pass the call to a human, or play a recording.


### What a dropped screener call costs


Cost What happens


A lost conversation The customer was seconds away from picking up, and the call ended first.


A spent call attempt For third-party agencies, Regulation F counts unanswered calls toward its limit of 7 calls in 7 days4,5. Each hang-up uses an attempt and produces no conversation.


A misidentified customer Some screeners read the customer’s name back. A system that hears the name can mistake the screener for the customer3 and start the account conversation with a machine.


## One account: AMD hung up 12 times, proAgent got through on its first call


On a large card issuer’s first-party collections program, a credit card account charged off in August 2024 owed about $1,500. Between September 11 and October 19, the dialer called the customer 12 times2. Each call reached an AI call screener, and each time AMD marked it as an answering machine and hung up after 16 or 17 seconds.

On October 22, proAgent called the same number once. The screener asked it to stay on the line at 15 seconds, and the customer picked up at 24. The call ran 8 minutes and 28 seconds and ended with the customer agreeing to pay the full balance, with no settlement and no discount. Both payments came in by October 30, and the account was paid in full.

## How proAgent handles a call screener


An AI agent has no idle time to protect, so it can wait on the line. proAgent works out who answered before it says anything that matters3.


- Every outbound call opens with a short greeting while proAgent identifies who answered.
- A separate screening model makes that decision, reading AMD as one signal among several.
- With a screener, the agent gives its name and company, holds, and hands over to the main AI agent when the customer picks up.
- With a voicemail greeting, it leaves a complete callback message after the beep.
- If your team already has a screener strategy or script, proAgent can follow it.


Behind your existing dialer, calls the dialer flags as a machine can be routed to proAgent instead of being disconnected.


## Screened calls will keep growing


Most new phones now come with call screening built in, and more customers get it every time they upgrade their phone. The share of outbound calls a screener answers will only grow, and so will the payments lost when a dialer hangs up.


When phones started answering for people


1. Oct. 2018 Google


Call Screen launches on the Pixel 3. Google Assistant answers an unknown caller, asks who is calling and why, and shows the owner a live transcript.


[The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/googles-pixel-3-will-use-ai-to-respond-to-telemarketer-calls) , Oct. 9, 2018


2. Feb. 2023 Samsung


Bixby Text Call arrives with the Galaxy S23. Bixby picks up the call and the owner reads and replies to the caller as text.


[Android Authority](https://www.androidauthority.com/bixby-text-call-3302264/)


3. Sept. 2025 Apple


iOS 26 adds Call Screening to the iPhone. Calls from unknown numbers are asked for a name and reason before the phone rings.


[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/snippet/3016749/ios-26-can-screen-calls-and-hold-your-place-in-call-center-queues/)


4. Sept. 2026 Meta


Muse, Meta’s personal AI assistant, starts placing calls to US businesses for consumers. Now the AI can sit on either end of the line.


[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/17/rival-ai-agents-instinct-and-metas-muse-both-add-the-ability-to-make-calls/) , Sept. 17, 2026;[Prodigal Research on personal AI assistants](https://www.prodigaltech.com/blog/the-customer-has-an-agent-now)
